records.name: Central Database Bottleneck
records.definition: Funneling all state through one shared database that becomes the system's scaling bottleneck.

records.name: Layer Leakage
records.definition: Letting an inner layer depend on an outer one, violating the direction of the dependency rule.

records.name: Layer Skipping
records.definition: Bypassing intermediate layers to call a distant layer directly, undermining the layering.

records.name: Monolithic Transform Function
records.definition: Doing all processing in one large transform instead of a series of composable filter stages.

records.name: Package by Technical Layer Only
records.definition: Organizing code by technical layer alone, scattering each feature across many packages.

records.name: Shared Monolithic Application
records.definition: Building one large shared application instead of composing independently-governed services.

records.name: Contract-Governed Service Reuse
records.definition: The ability to reuse services across an enterprise through well-defined contracts.

records.name: Database-Bottleneck Removal
records.definition: The ability to eliminate the shared-database bottleneck by holding state in distributed memory.

records.name: Decentralized Ownership
records.definition: The ability for separate teams to own, deploy and evolve their services independently.

records.name: External System Isolation
records.definition: The ability to isolate the core from external systems behind adapter boundaries.

records.name: Framework Independence
records.definition: The ability to keep business rules independent of any particular framework.

records.name: Independent Stage Testing
records.definition: The ability to test each filter stage in isolation from the rest of the pipeline.

records.name: Infrastructure Independence

distinctFrom.reason: Infrastructure independence keeps the core free of the platform it runs on, while external system isolation keeps the systems it calls behind adapters.

records.definition: The ability to keep the core independent of the infrastructure it runs on.

records.name: Locality of Change
records.definition: The ability to make a feature's changes in one place because its code is grouped together.

records.name: Reorderable Stages

distinctFrom.reason: Reorderable stages can be rearranged or recombined, while independent stage testing exercises each stage alone.

records.definition: The ability to reorder or recombine independent processing stages.

records.name: Structured Code Organization
records.definition: The ability to organize code predictably by assigning each responsibility to a layer.

records.name: Transactional Simplicity
records.definition: The ability to use straightforward local transactions when all state lives in one process.

records.name: Adapters
records.definition: Components that translate between a core's ports and the specific external technologies behind them.

records.name: Boundaries
records.definition: The requirement that clear boundaries separate the concentric layers of the system.

records.name: Component Boundaries
records.definition: The requirement that each component expose a well-defined boundary and interface.

records.name: Dependency Rule

distinctFrom.reason: The dependency rule fixes the direction dependencies point, while boundaries are the lines between the layers they cross.
The dependency rule governs direction, while use cases are the application operations held in their own layer.

records.definition: The requirement that source-code dependencies point only inward, toward higher-level policy.

records.name: Domain Core
records.definition: The requirement that pure domain logic occupy the core, isolated from external concerns.

records.name: Layer Separation
records.definition: The requirement that responsibilities be divided into distinct, ordered layers.

records.name: Ports

distinctFrom.reason: Ports are the interfaces at the edge of the core, while the domain core is the logic those interfaces enclose.

records.definition: The requirement that the core define abstract interface points through which all external interaction passes.

records.name: Replicated In-Memory State
records.definition: The requirement that application state be kept in replicated in-memory grids rather than a central store.

records.name: Unified Deployment Boundary
records.definition: The requirement that the whole application build and deploy as one unit.

records.name: Uniform Stage Interface
records.definition: The requirement that every stage share one interface so stages can be composed freely.

records.name: Use Cases

distinctFrom.reason: Use cases are the operations in the application layer, while boundaries are the lines separating that layer from the others.

records.definition: The requirement that application operations be captured as explicit use cases in their own layer.

records.name: Anemic Layers
records.definition: The degree to which strict layering produces thin pass-through layers that add indirection without logic.

records.name: End-to-End Traceability
records.definition: The degree to which decomposing flow into independent filters makes tracing a request end to end harder.

records.name: Feature Cohesion
records.definition: The degree to which all code serving one feature is grouped together rather than scattered by layer.

records.name: Independent Scaling
records.definition: The degree to which a single deployable unit prevents scaling parts of the system independently.

records.name: Initial Complexity
records.definition: The degree of upfront structural complexity introduced by defining ports and adapters.

records.name: Integration Overhead
records.definition: The degree of effort required to wire independently-developed components together.

records.name: Operational Simplicity
records.definition: The degree to which a single deployable unit keeps building, deploying, and operating simple.

records.name: Shared Technical Concerns
records.definition: The degree to which grouping by feature complicates sharing cross-cutting technical code.

records.name: Introduce Port
records.definition: A technique for declaring an interface owned by the core that names what it needs from the outside world.

records.name: Extract Adapter
records.definition: A technique for moving the code that talks to a framework, vendor or protocol into an adapter behind a port.

records.name: Move Framework Outward
records.definition: A technique for removing framework types and annotations from the core and confining them to adapters.

records.name: Repackage by Feature
records.definition: A technique for moving the code of one feature from technical-layer folders into one folder of its own.
